title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a preregistered, deterministic paired experiment (N=120 intent→configuration tasks) that compared an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) against an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). A single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) produced one shared initial candidate per task (model_calls_used = 120). A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applied intent-constraint and workflow-policy checks and would trigger ≤1 repair iteration only if validator-detected violations occurred. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120 = 1.00; guarded success = 120/120 = 1.00 (contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0). Artifact-derived concordance: normalized_response == normalized_reference for 120/120 shared initial candidates (100%). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes (no validator-detected violations). We incorporate reviewer-requested artifact-resolvable clarifications: shared-generation semantics (one shared candidate per paired task), repair-trigger logic (repairs conditional on validator.violation_count>0), and an artifact-grounded explanation for why the confirmatory test is uninformative (no discordant pairs → statistical degeneracy). We discuss the ceiling/null outcome, the inference limits imposed by the shared-generation design, task coverage, and external-validity constraints of this synthetic deterministic harness. Key archived artifacts (full manifest archived): execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/model_configuration.json; execution/task_manifest.jsonl; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; preregistration CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1.

sections.introduction: Automating network-configuration tasks with generative LLMs promises operational speed but risks semantic regressions: syntactically plausible commands can violate required workflows (e.g., make-before-break, shutdown→change→restore) and cause outages. Prior work therefore advocates tool-augmented pipelines—generate→validate→repair loops, digital twins, or veto layers—that execute or formally check generated candidates before enactment. We ask a focused, preregistered question: does inserting an executable emulator-based validator into a generate→validate→repair loop reduce semantic (network-level) failures of LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? To isolate validator/repair effects from generation variance we used a deterministic, paired design with a single shared initial generation per task. We report artifact-backed execution and analysis for N=120 paired tasks (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) and explicitly interpret a narrow ceiling/null outcome in the context of design choices and external-validity limits.
sections.related_work: Recent benchmarks and surveys show that evaluating only syntactic or command-level correctness underestimates operational failure modes; executable, emulator- or verifier-backed evaluations reveal semantic errors and motivate guardrails. Representative efforts propose generate→validate→repair chains, digital twins, and bounded-autonomy guardrails to catch make-before-break or other workflow violations. These works motivate our confirmatory paired test that isolates validator/repair efficacy when the same LLM candidate is evaluated with and without the guarded repair step. We position this experiment as a constrained, preregistered probe of validator utility under a deterministic harness—not as a general multi-model or production-readiness claim.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study is preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) and used a paired binary design. Exactly N=120 intent→configuration tasks were deterministically generated and assigned into three topology classes per the preregistration (40 tasks each: edge, core, leaf–spine). For each task we produced a single shared initial candidate from gpt-5-mini (initial_generation_calls_per_task=1; independent_condition_generation=false). Conditions: baseline = apply LLM candidate to emulator; guarded = subject the same candidate to an executable validator and attempt ≤1 repair iteration only if validator.violation_count>0. Validator and tooling: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) performed intent-constraint and workflow checks (examples: make-before-break, required shutdown→change→restore). Model/configuration: all generations used gpt-5-mini under the frozen run configuration archived in execution/model_configuration.json; execution accounting and manifests are archived. Primary estimand and inferential plan: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline tested by exact two-sided McNemar (alpha=0.05); bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples (seed=1729). Inclusion/exclusion: per preregistration, technical/instrumentation failures would be excluded; none occurred. Repair-trigger logic (artifact-resolved): a guarded repair was invoked only if validator.violation_count>0; archived validator traces show repair_applied=false for all guarded episodes because violation_count=0 for each archived scoring JSON.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: planned_episode_count = 240 (120 pairs); completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared initial generation per pair). Scoring and concordance: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every tested candidate valid; artifact-derived concordance (normalized_response == normalized_reference) = 120/120 = 100% for the shared initial candidates (scoring JSONs archived under execution/scoring/). Contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0; observed success rates baseline = 120/120 = 1.00; guarded = 120/120 = 1.00. Confirmatory analysis: paired-difference estimate = 0.00; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Repair activity: repair_applied = false for every guarded episode (no validator-detected violations), so preregistered secondary metrics about repair frequency are vacuous. Missingness and contamination: analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 and analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flags.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and statistical degeneracy: the run produced a narrow null (ceiling) outcome because the baseline generation already produced emulator-valid candidates for every paired task; there were no discordant pairs. In McNemar's test the absence of discordant pairs degenerates the test—p=1.0 and CI=[0,0] reflect this degeneracy and do not constitute evidence of equivalence or of the guarded pipeline's general irrelevance. Shared-generation design tradeoff: using one shared initial candidate per task was an explicit design choice to isolate validator/repair efficacy from generation randomness (it prevents attributing differences to stochastic generation). That choice reduced sensitivity to remedies that would rely on repairing independently generated, invalid baseline outputs: had independent per-condition generations been used, the guarded pipeline could have been credited for repairing baseline-invalid candidates. Task coverage and difficulty: topology assignment followed the preregistered 3×40 split (edge/core/leaf–spine = 40 tasks each). Representative entries in the archived task_manifest show difficulty.level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}; the full task_manifest is archived for inspection (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Why repairs were never applied: validator traces record violation_count = 0 for every shared initial candidate; because repairs are conditional on violation_count>0, repair_applied remained false across all guarded episodes. External validity and operational implications: this controlled synthetic harness and frozen prompt/model produced a ceiling result; it does not imply guarded loops are unnecessary in realistic, heterogeneous, adversarial, or multi-vendor deployments. Operational recommendation: guarded generate→validate→repair architectures remain prudent safety measures; follow-up experiments should (a) use independent per-condition generation to test repair effectiveness on discrepant generation, (b) test multiple models and prompt variants, (c) expand repair budgets and strategies, and (d) use higher-fidelity multi-vendor validators or production-rooted incident corpora to probe real-world utility.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline to an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness and a single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator (n_11=120), yielding a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00]). Artifact-resolved clarifications requested by peer review are incorporated: the run used a shared initial generation per task (model_calls_used = 120), guarded repairs were conditional on validator.violation_count>0 (none occurred; repair_applied = false), and task topology was assigned as preregistered (40 tasks per topology class). The result is narrowly scoped: it documents a ceiling effect on this curated synthetic task bank and does not generalize to production heterogeneity. The archived manifests and scoring traces permit reproducible inspection (see minimal filenames below); future work must relax shared-generation constraints, widen model/prompt diversity, and use higher-fidelity validators to assess operational value of guarded repair loops more robustly.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but necessarily simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
